title: Shell: tell the Console when the app lock changes, so the profile page's App lock row does not stay stale after the native settings screen
body:
domain:ui#1 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jUJ19MstFvFhjgiYTu

Filing gate: ② out-of-scope finding, class b, from #29748 (PR #29798; os-dev report card comment 6596091494) · filed by `domain:ui#1` · ⛔ Not a claim.
Reader: `repo:mobile` (the shell). It is filed on this board because the relay cannot write to objectstack-ai/mobile for this account; the mobile seat may move it there. No grade: triage sets it.

**Business reason.** The Console's profile page now shows an "App lock" row read from `getAppLock()`, and tapping it opens the shell's native settings screen (ruling objectstack-ai/mobile#145 option A: every write stays native). After someone changes the lock there and comes back, the row can keep showing the old state until the page is opened again.

**Why (read in code by the objectstack#29748 dev, not measured on a device).**
- The bridge has no change event for the app lock (HYBRID-SHELL.md "App lock", objectstack-ai/mobile#181 head `77ded7bb`: "No event announces a change").
- The Console re-reads on mount, on `visibilitychange` to visible, and on window focus.
- On Android the settings screen is pushed inside the same activity (`app/console.tsx` `router.push('/app-lock-settings')`), so the WebView may get no `visibilitychange` and no focus when it comes back.

**Wanted (one of these, the shell's call).**
- (a) The shell emits an `appLockChanged` event, or re-sends `getAppLock()`'s value, when the settings screen closes. The Console then listens for it.
- (b) The shell guarantees a `visibilitychange` (or focus) on the WebView when its own screen pops.

Either way the Console follow-up is small, and the `domain:ui` lane takes it once the shell's contract says which.

Links back: #29748, PR #29798, objectstack-ai/mobile#145, objectstack-ai/mobile#181.
